verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तस्मिंस्तु कर्णार्जुनयोर्विमर्दे दग्धस्य रौद्रेऽहनि विद्रुतस्य । बभूव रूपं कुरुसृञ्जयानां बलस्य बाणोन्मथितस्य कीदृक् ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said How did Kuru and Srinjaya army look, when on that dreadful day, it was assailed and consumed with arrows in that encounter between Karna and Arjuna and while it was flying from the action.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              शृणु राजन्नवहितो यथा वृत्तो महाक्षयः । घोरो मनुष्यदेहानामाजौ च गजवाजिनाम् ॥२॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Listen, attentively, O king, to the onslaught of men, horses and elephants in that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र कर्णे हते पार्थः सिंहनाद‌मथाकरोत् । तदा तव सुतान्राजन्नाविवेश महद्भयम् ॥३॥
verses.english: When after Karna's fall Partha sent up leonine war-cries your sons were possessed by a mighty fear.

verses.sanskrit: न सन्धातुमनीकानि न चैवाशु पराक्रमे । आसीद्बुद्धिर्हते कर्णे तव योधस्य कर्हिचित् ॥४॥
verses.english: After Kanra's fall no warrior of your side had a heart of rallying your troops or displaying his prowess.

verses.sanskrit: वणिजो नावि भिन्नायामगाधे विप्लवे यथा । अपारे पारमिच्छन्तो हते द्वीपे किरीटिना ॥५॥
verses.english: On their main stay being destroyed by Arjuna they were like merchants, whose vessels had been wrecked on the deep main, desirous of crossing it.

verses.sanskrit: सूतपुत्रे हते राजन् वित्रस्ताः शस्त्रविक्षताः । अनाथा नाथमिच्छन्तो मृगाः सिंहैरिवार्दिताः ॥६॥
verses.english: After the destruction of the charioteer's son, the Kauravas, terrified and wounded with arrows, having no lord and seeking refuge, locked like a herd of elephants pursued by lion.

verses.sanskrit: भग्नशृंगा वृषा यद्वद्भग्नदंष्ट्रा इवोरगाः । प्रत्यपायामसायान्हे निर्जिताः सव्यसाचिना ॥७॥
verses.english: Discomfited by Savyasachin that evening they took to their heels like bulls with broken horns or serpents with wounded fangs.

verses.sanskrit: हतप्रवीरा विध्वस्ता निकृत्ता निशितैः शरैः । सूतपुत्रे हते राजन् पुत्रास्ते दुद्रुवुर्भयात् ॥८॥
verses.english: Having the beast of their heroes killed, their soldiers all routed and themselves sounded with sharp arrows your sons, on the fall of Karna, fled away in fear.

verses.sanskrit: विस्रस्तयन्त्रकवचाः कांदिग्भूता विचेतसः । अन्योन्यमवमृद्नन्तो वीक्षमाणा भयार्दिताः ॥९॥
verses.english: Deprived of their coats of mail and weapons, unconscious of the right direction and bewildered they crushed one another in their flight and cast fearful looks upon one another.

verses.sanskrit: मामेव नूनं बीभत्सुर्मामेव च वृकोदरः । अभियातीति मन्वानाः पेतुर्मम्लुश्च संभ्रमात् ॥१०॥
verses.english: on The Kauravas, pale with fear, thought “Vibhatsa is following me, Vrikodaras is pursing me" and fell down as they fled.

verses.sanskrit: हयानन्ये गजानन्ये रथानन्ये महारथाः । आरुह्य जवसंपन्नाः पदातीन्प्रजहुर्भयात् ॥११॥
verses.english: Thus fled away in fear all the great carwarriors some on cars, some on horses, some on elephants and some on foot.

verses.sanskrit: कुञ्जरैः स्यन्दनाः क्षुण्णाः सादिनश्च महारथैः । पदातिसंघाश्चाश्वौघैः पलायद्भिर्भयार्दितैः ॥१२॥
verses.english: In their fearful fight cars were shattered by elephants, the cavalry were crushed by carwarriors and the infantry were trampled down by horses.

verses.sanskrit: व्यालतस्करसंकीर्णे सार्थहीना यथा वने । सूतपुत्रे हते राजंस्तव योधास्तथाऽभवन् ॥१३॥
verses.english: After the fall of Karna your warrior behaved like men, having no protector in a forest abounding in beasts of prey and robbers.

verses.sanskrit: हतारोहा यथा नागाश्छिन्नहस्ता यथा नराः । सर्वे पार्थमयं लोकं संपश्यन्तो भयार्दिताः ॥१४॥
verses.english: They behaved like elephants without riders and men without arms. Stricken with fear they thought that the entire universe was filled with Partha.

verses.sanskrit: संप्रेक्ष्य द्रवतः सर्वान् भीमसेनभयार्दितान् । दुर्योधनोऽथ स्वं सूतं हाहाकृत्वेद‌मब्रवीत् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Seeing them thus take to their heels in fear of Bhimasena and his soldiers leave the battle field by thousands, Duryodhana, bewailing, said to his driver.

verses.sanskrit: नातिक्रमेच्च मां पार्थो धनुष्पाणिमवस्थितम् । जघने सर्वसैन्यानां शनैरश्वान्प्रचोदय ॥१६॥
verses.english: "Partha will not be able to go beyond me standing bow in hand. Drive my horses behind all the troops.

verses.sanskrit: युध्यमानं हि कौन्तेयं हनिष्यामि न संशयः । नोत्सहेन्मामतिक्रान्तुं वेलामिव महोदधिः ॥१७॥
verses.english: If I fight in the rear of my army forsooth the son of Kunti will not be able to approach me as the ocean is unable to go beyond its banks.

verses.sanskrit: अद्यार्जुनं सगोविन्दं मानिनं च वृकोदरम् । हन्यां शिष्टांस्तथा शत्रून् कर्णस्यानृण्यमाप्नुयाम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Killing Arjuna, Govinda, the haughty Vrikodara and my other enemies I will repay the debt I owe to Karna."

verses.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा कुरुराजस्य शूरार्यसदृशं वचः । सूतो हेमपरिच्छन्नान् शनैरश्वानचोदयत् ॥१९॥
verses.english: Hearing the words of the Kuru Chief becoming a hero and an honorable man the driver slowly drove his horses adorned with golden trappings.

verses.sanskrit: रथाश्वनागहीनास्तु पादातास्तव मारिष । पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्रा युद्धायैव व्यवस्थिताः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then deprived of cars, cavalry and clephants, twenty-five thousand warriors of your army addressed themselves for fighting on foot.

verses.sanskrit: तान् भीमसेनः संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः । बलेन चतुरङ्गेण संवृत्याजघ्नतुः शरैः ॥२१॥
verses.english: Then worked up with anger Bhimasena and Prisata's son Dhristadyumna encircled them with four kinds of forces and began to strike them with their arrows.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्ययुध्यन्त समरे भीमसेनं सपार्षतम् । पार्थपार्षतयोश्चान्ये जगृहुस्तत्र नामनी ॥२२॥
verses.english: Your warriors also fought with Bhimasena and Prisata's son. Some of them challenged both the heroes by calling them by name.

verses.sanskrit: अक्रुध्यत रणे भीमस्तैस्तदा पर्यवस्थितैः । सोऽवतीर्य रथात्तूर्णं गदापाणिरयुध्यत ॥२३॥
verses.english: Thereat Bhima was worked up with anger. Coming down from his car with a mace in his hand he fought with those warriors standing for battle.

verses.sanskrit: न तान्रथस्थो भूमिष्ठान् धर्मापेक्षी वृकोदरः । योधयामास कौन्तेयो भुजवीर्यव्यपाश्रयः ॥२४॥
verses.english: Following the rules of a fair fight, Kunti's son Vrikodara alighted from his car and depending upon the strength of his own arms he began to fight with them on foot.

verses.sanskrit: जातरूपपरिच्छन्नां प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम् । अवधीत्तावकान्सर्वान् दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः ॥२५॥
verses.english: Taking up his heavy golden mace he made a havoc on them like Death himself armed with his bludgeon.

verses.sanskrit: पदातिनोऽपि संत्यक्त्वा प्रियं जीवितमात्मनः । भीममभ्यद्रवन्संख्ये पतङ्गा ज्वलनं यथा ॥२६॥
verses.english: Then worked up with anger and heedless of their lives the Kuru soldiers rushed upon Bhima like insects falling upon a burning fire.

verses.sanskrit: आसाद्य भीमसेनं तु संरब्धा युद्धदुर्मदाः । विनेशुः सहसा दृष्ट्वा भूतग्रामा इवान्तकम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: The maddened warriors, whom it was difficult to vanquish in battle, perished in no time like creatures on seeing Death himself,

verses.sanskrit: श्येनवद्विचरन् भीमो गदाहस्तो महाबलः । पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्रांस्तावकानवपोथयत् ॥२८॥
verses.english: Armed with his mace the powerful Bhima moved about like hawk and killed those twenty five thousand warriors.

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा तत्पुरुषानीकं भीमः सत्यपराक्रमः । धृष्टद्युम्नं पुरस्कृत्य तस्थौ तत्र महाबलः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Having killed that heroic army Bhima, of great strength, whom it was difficult to defeat in battle, stood there with Dhristadyumna before him.

verses.sanskrit: धनञ्जयो रथानीकमभ्यवर्तत वीर्यवान् । माद्रीपुत्रौ तु शकुनिं सात्यकिश्च महारथः ॥३०॥
verses.english: Drawing his bow Gandiva known all over the three worlds the highly energetic Dhananjaya rushed against your car-warriors.

verses.sanskrit: जवेनाभ्यपतन् हृष्टा घ्नन्तो दौर्योधनं बलम् । तस्याश्वसादीन्सुबहूंस्ते निहत्य शितैः शरैः ॥३१॥
verses.english: The energetic Dhananjaya Dhananjaya proceeded against the remaining car warriors of the Kuru away. Nakula, Sahadeva and Satyaki with great pleasure proceeded against Shakuni and killed the soldiers of Subala's son.

verses.sanskrit: समभ्यधावंस्त्वरितास्तत्र युद्धमभून्महत् । धनञ्जयोऽपि चाभ्येत्य रथानीकं तव प्रभो ॥३२॥
verses.english: Having killed with sharp arrows his cavalry and elephants they attacked Shakuni himself upon which a great encounter took place.

verses.sanskrit: विश्रुतं त्रिषु लोकेषु गाण्डीवं विक्षिपन् धनुः । कृष्णसारथिमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा श्वेतहयं रथम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: In the meantime proceeding against your car-warriors Dhananjaya twanged his bow Gandiva known all over the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनं चापि योद्धारं त्वदीयाः प्राद्रवन्भयात् । विप्रहीणरथाश्चैव शरैश्च परिकर्षिताः ॥३४॥
verses.english: Seeing his car drawn by white horses and driven by Krishna himself and Arjuna standing on it your soldiers fled away in fear.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्राः कालमार्छन् पदातयः । हत्वा तान् पुरुषव्याघ्रः पञ्चालानां महारथः ॥३५॥
verses.english: Twenty-five thousand foot soldiers, deprived of cars, were killed there with arrows (by Bhima and Dhristadyumna).

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रः पाञ्चालराजस्य धृष्टद्युम्नो महामनाः । भीमसेनं पुरस्कृत्य न चिरात्प्रत्यदृश्यत ॥३६॥
verses.english: Having killed them that best of men, the foremost of car-warriors, the heroic son of Panchala king Dhristadyumna again appeared in view with Bhima before him. That great bowman, the destroyer of the enemies, looked there exceedingly beautiful.

verses.sanskrit: महाधनुर्धरः श्रीमानमित्रगणतापनः । पारावतसवर्णाश्वं कोविदारमयध्वजम् ॥३७॥
धृष्टद्युम्नं रणे दृष्ट्वा त्वदीयाः प्राद्रवन् भयात् । गान्धारराजं शीघ्रास्त्रमनुसृत्य यशस्विनौ ॥३८॥
verses.english: Seeing Dhristadyumna's car, drawn by horses white as pigeons and bearing a standard made of a Kovidara tree the Kuru soldiers fled away in dismay.

verses.sanskrit: न चिरात्प्रत्यदृश्येतां माद्रीपुत्रौ ससात्यकी । चेकितानः शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष ॥३९॥
verses.english: Having pursued the light-handed king of Gandharvas the illustrious twins and Satyaki again appeared (amongst the Pandavas.)

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा त्वदीयं सुमहत्सैन्यं शंखांस्तथाऽधमन् । ते सर्वे तावकान् प्रेक्ष्य द्रवतोऽपि पराङ्मुखान् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Having killed your huge army Chikitan, Shikhandin and the five sons of Draupadi blew their conchs.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यवर्तन्त संरब्धान् वृषाञ्जित्वा यथा वृषाः । सेनावशेषं तं दृष्ट्वा तव सैन्यस्य पाण्डवः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Although they saw your soldiers flying away from the battle-field those heroes pursued i them like bulls pursuing other angry bulls.

verses.sanskrit: व्यवस्थितः सव्यसाची चुक्रोध बलवान्नृप । धनञ्जयो रथानीकमभ्यवर्तत वीर्यवान् ॥४२॥
verses.english: Still seeing a portion of your army standing for battle Savyasachin was filled with anger.

verses.sanskrit: विश्रुतं त्रिषु लोकेषु व्याक्षिपद्गाण्डिवं धनुः । तत एनाञ्शरव्रातैः सहसा समवाकिरत् ॥४३॥
verses.english: All on a sudden he covered your soldiers with arrows. The dust covered the directions and nothing was discernible.

verses.sanskrit: तमसा संवृतेनाथ न स्म किंचिद्व्यदृश्यत । अन्धकारीकृते लोके रजोभूते महीतले ॥४४॥
verses.english: When the earth was thus covered with dust and all the quarters were enshrouded with darkness your soldiers, O king, fled away on all sides in dismay.

verses.sanskrit: योधाः सर्वे महाराज तावकाः प्राद्रवन्भयात् । संभज्यमाने सैन्ये तु कुरुराजो विशांपते ॥४५॥
verses.english: When his army was thus routed your son, the Kuru king, rushed against his enemies who were proceeding against him.

verses.sanskrit: परानभिमुखांश्चैव सुतस्ते समुपाद्रवत् । ततो दुर्योधनः सर्वानाजुहावाथ पाण्डवान् ॥४६॥
युद्धाय भरतश्रेष्ठ देवानिव पुरा बलिः । त एनमभिगर्जन्तः सहिताः समुपाद्रवन् ॥४७॥
verses.english: Duryodhana then challenged all the Pandavas in battle as did the Asura Bali the celestials in days of yore.

verses.sanskrit: नानाशस्त्रभृतः क्रुद्धा भर्त्सयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः । दुर्योधनोऽप्यसंभ्रान्तस्तान्रणे निशितैः शरैः ॥४८॥
verses.english: Thereat all the Pandava warriors rushed in a body upon Duryodhana, hurled various weapons and chastised him again and again.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रावधीत्ततः क्रुद्धः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । तत्सैन्यं पाण्डवेयानां योधयामास सर्वतः ॥४९॥
verses.english: Worked up with anger, however, Duryodhana killed his enemies, in hundreds and thousands with keen arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव पुत्रस्य पौरुषम् । यदेकः सहितान्सर्वान् रणेऽयुध्यत पाण्डवान् ॥५०॥
verses.english: Wonderful was the prowess your son exhibited on that occasion for alone and with none to help him he fought with all the Pandavas in a body.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽपश्यन्महात्मा स स्वसैन्यं भृशदुःखितम् । ततोऽवस्थाप्य राजेन्द्र कृतबुद्धिस्तवात्मजः ॥५१॥
verses.english: Duryodhana then saw that all his soldiers were assailed with wounds and about to flee but had not gone very far from the scene of action.

verses.sanskrit: हर्षयन्निव तान् योधानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । न तं देशं प्रपश्यामि यत्र याता भयार्दिताः ॥५२॥
verses.english: Rallying his soldiers and cheering them up your son, who was bent upon keeping his honor, said-

verses.sanskrit: गतानां यत्र वै मोक्षः पाण्डवात्किं गतेन वः । अल्पं च बलमेतेषां कृष्णौ च भृशविक्षतौ ॥५३॥
verses.english: There is no spot on earth or on mountain, I see, where if you go the Pandavas will not kill you. What is the use of your flying away?

verses.sanskrit: अद्य सर्वान्हनिष्यामि ध्रुवो हि विजयो भवेत् । विप्रयातांस्तु वो भिन्नान् पाण्डवाः कृतकिल्बिषान् ॥५४॥
verses.english: The Pandava army is very small now. The two Krishnas have been assailed with wounds. If we all stand for battle we will surely win victory.

verses.sanskrit: अनुसृत्य वधिष्यन्ति श्रेयान्नः समरे वधः । सुखं सांग्रामिको मृत्युः क्षत्रधर्मेण युध्यताम् ॥५५॥
verses.english: If we however fly away disconcerted the sinsul Pandavas will pursue us and kill us all. It is better therefore that we should die in battle.

verses.sanskrit: मृतो दुःखं न जानीते प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते । शृणुध्वं क्षत्रियाः सर्वे यावन्तः स्थ समागताः ॥५६॥
verses.english: Happy is the death in the battle-field. Follow your Kshatriya duties and fight. The dead know no misery. They however enjoy eternal bliss hereafter.

verses.sanskrit: यदा शूरं च भीरुं च मारयत्यन्तको यमः । को न मूढो न युध्येत मादृशः क्षत्रियव्रतः ॥५७॥
verses.english: Listen therefore, O Kshatriyas who have assembled here. While death does not spare a hero or a coward what foolish Kshatriya is there who would not fight?

verses.sanskrit: द्विषतो भीमसेनस्य क्रुद्धस्य वशमेष्यथ । पितामहैराचरितं न धर्मं हातुमर्हथ ॥५८॥
verses.english: Will you place yourselves under the power of our enemy Bhima? It is not proper that you should neglect the duties followed by your fathers and grand-fathers.

verses.sanskrit: न ह्यधर्मोऽस्ति पापीयान् क्षत्रियस्य पलायनात् । न युद्धधर्माच्छ्रेयो हि पन्थाः स्वर्गस्य कौरवाः । अचिरेण हता लोकान् सद्यो योधाः समश्नुत ॥५९॥
verses.english: There is no sin greater to a Kshatriya than flight from the battle-field. There is no more blessed road to heaven than battle; killed in battle therefore, O Kshatriyas, enjoy heaven in no time.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              एवं ब्रुवति पुत्रे ते सैनिका भृशविक्षताः । अनवेक्ष्यैव तद्वाक्यं प्राद्रवन्सर्वतो दिशः ॥६०॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Though your son gave vent to those words the Kuru soldiers greatly wounded fled away on all sides caring not for his speech.
